name: Hang Nadim International Airport
before:
Batam's airport, in the Riau Islands, and the main way in and out of the island alongside the ferries. Singapore is about 30 km to the north.

The runway is the striking thing. At 4,025 metres it is the largest in Indonesia and second longest in Southeast Asia, and it takes 747s, 777s and the A380. That is because it was developed to handle aircraft diverting from Singapore Changi in emergencies or bad weather, not because of its own traffic. The site covers 1,800 hectares of which only about 40 per cent is normally in use.

It has run 24 hours a day since May 2014 and is second busiest in Sumatra after Medan, with flights to Jakarta, Surabaya, Medan and Balikpapan, international services to Malaysia and seasonal Hajj flights.

Lion Air has built up a base here partly because Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta is so congested.

The airport shares its facilities with an Indonesian Air Force base and has a growing aircraft maintenance operation.
after:
Batam's airport, in the Riau Islands. Singapore Changi Airport is about 30 km to the north west.

The runway is the striking thing. At 4,025 metres it is the longest in Indonesia, and it takes wide bodies up to a Boeing 747. Singapore-bound flights divert here when the weather at Changi is bad.

Flights run to Jakarta, Surabaya, Medan and Balikpapan. International flights go to Malaysia and South Korea.

It also has a growing aircraft maintenance operation, run by the Lion Air group's Batam Aero Technic.

claims.claim: Singapore Changi Airport is about 30 km to the north west
claims.inAfter: Singapore Changi Airport is about 30 km to the north west.
claims.note: Was 'Singapore is about 30 km to the north'. The 30 km is Wikipedia's distance to Changi Airport, and both coordinate sets agree: 29.0 km at 331 degrees (OurAirports) and 30.1 km at 332 degrees (Wikipedia's coordinates), which is north west on the eight-point compass. The coordinates check had measured the figure from Batam's centre, which it does not describe.

claims.inAfter: At 4,025 metres it is the longest in Indonesia
claims.note: The regulator verifies the runway at 4,025 by 45 m (OurAirports rounds it to 4,029 m). On OurAirports' runway data for every Indonesian airport with scheduled flights it is the longest, ahead of Kualanamu (3,750 m) and Soekarno-Hatta (3,660 m). Wikipedia's 'largest runway' means longest.

claims.note: Was 'it takes 747s, 777s and the A380'. The regulator's critical aircraft, the largest type the airport is designed for, is the Boeing 747-400, and it classes the airport 4E, the code for 747-size aircraft. The A380 is a larger code F type, so it is cut; the 777 rests on Wikipedia alone.

claims.claim: Singapore-bound flights divert here when the weather at Changi is bad
claims.inAfter: Singapore-bound flights divert here when the weather at Changi is bad.
claims.note: Was 'That is because it was developed to handle aircraft diverting from Singapore Changi in emergencies or bad weather, not because of its own traffic.' Antara (July 2013) reports two Singapore-bound aircraft diverting here in heavy rain at Changi and quotes the airport: when Changi's weather is bad, many planes divert to Hang Nadim. The claim that the runway was built for that purpose rests on Wikipedia's lead alone, and Wikipedia's own history says the runway was extended in anticipation of an international hub (see the cuts).

quote: Two Singapore-bound Airbus planes diverted their flights to Hang Nadim Airport in Batam island as heavy rains fell in Changi Airport on Friday, a spokesman said.

Wikipedia: the Lion Air Group set up Batam Aero Technic in 2014 and built its maintenance facilities at the airport, which is 'gradually transforming into a hub for aircraft maintenance'.

claims.wasBefore: Lion Air has built up a base here partly because Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta is so congested.
claims.why: The flying base and its reason rest on Wikipedia alone (Lion Air's release on Kontan's press-release site answered a CloudFront 'Request blocked' 403). What two sources do confirm is the Lion Air group's maintenance base, Batam Aero Technic, which is kept (see above).

claims.claim: shares its facilities with an Indonesian Air Force base
claims.wasBefore: The airport shares its facilities with an Indonesian Air Force base and has a growing aircraft maintenance operation.
claims.why: The Air Force base (Lanud Hang Nadim) rests on Wikipedia alone: its source, RRI's report, answered with a Cloudflare check and was not tried again. The maintenance operation is kept (see above).

sources.quote: Hang Nadim International Airport also share its facility with Hang Nadim Air Force Base

claims.claim: operator, Terminal 1 renovation and Terminal 2 plan
claims.why: Held back: the airport is run under a public-private partnership by PT Bandara Internasional Batam (the operator's own site), the consortium Wikipedia describes as Angkasa Pura I, Incheon International Airport Corporation and Wijaya Karya (awarded March 2021, 25 years). Batam Pos (12 July 2025) quotes its chief executive: Terminal 1 has been fully renovated and a Terminal 2 for up to 10 million passengers is planned for 2026. It replaces nothing in the old text, and the Terminal 2 date has no source from the last 12 months.
